texts:
Websites have mascots. three.ws pages have agents that physically show up.

This one swings in from off screen on a rope, hits the button, watches it wobble back into place, and then just hangs there. A real 3D character rendered over the page in WebGL, not a video.

It is one of a set of interaction prototypes for 3D agents on ordinary web pages: entrances, pick-ups, face mocap and more.

Play with all of them: three.ws/demos/agents

issues.problem: The opening is a generalization and contrast setup rather than the strongest true statement or mechanism; it reads as a machine-written contrast reframe and wastes the first 280 characters on a vague observation instead of the feature itself.
issues.fix: Replace with the mechanism lead: "She swings in from off screen on a rope, knocks the button sideways, and hangs there."

issues.quote: three.ws pages have agents that physically show up.
issues.problem: Not a checkable mechanism; the first line should carry the strongest true statement about how it works, and "physically show up" is vague.
issues.fix: Follow the opening with "A real 3D agent rendered over the page in WebGL, not a video."

issues.problem: Colloquial and less precise than the source text "she dangles before letting go" and the reel caption "Then she hangs around."
issues.fix: Change to "and dangles" or "and hangs around."
